reports.report: I modeled the problem by iterating over all possible sets of 5 vertices from the 101 vertices of the regular 101-gon. The interior angle at a vertex depends on the sum of the lengths of the two arcs between its adjacent vertices. An angle is acute if the sum of these arc lengths exceeds 101/2. By iterating over all possible arc length 5-tuples (d1, d2, d3, d4, d5) that sum to 101 and each d_i >= 1, I identified the 5-tuples that result in exactly two acute angles. Summing the number of vertex sets for each such 5-tuple yielded 48,500,200.

def solve():
    n = 101
    count = 0
    # d1+d2+d3+d4+d5 = n, di >= 1
    # S1 = d5+d1, S2 = d1+d2, S3 = d2+d3, S4 = d3+d4, S5 = d4+d5
    # exactly two of Si >= 51
    
    # We can iterate over d1, d2, d3, d4 and d5 will be n - (d1+d2+d3+d4)
    # The sum of d1+d2+d3+d4+d5 = 101, so d1+d2+d3+d4 <= 100
    # Also d5 >= 1, so d1+d2+d3+d4 <= 100
    
    for d1 in range(1, n-3):
        for d2 in range(1, n-d1-2):
            for d3 in range(1, n-d1-d2-1):
                for d4 in range(1, n-d1-d2-d3):
                    d5 = n - (d1 + d2 + d3 + d4)
                    
                    s1 = d5 + d1
                    s2 = d1 + d2
                    s3 = d2 + d3
                    s4 = d3 + d4
                    s5 = d4 + d5
                    
                    acute_count = 0
                    if s1 >= 51: acute_count += 1
                    if s2 >= 51: acute_count += 1
                    if s3 >= 51: acute_count += 1
                    if s4 >= 51: acute_count += 1
                    if s5 >= 51: acute_count += 1
                    
                    if acute_count == 2:
                        count += d5
    return count

print(solve())
